items.rationale: Surge damage is covered under 2.3.3 and the speakers were physically damaged. The 50% reduction under 2.3.3 applies because nothing was on a surge protector and no waiver endorsement exists. Earlier cases with no protection put speakers at about 250-525 before the reduction, so I take roughly 300 as the half-payment figure.

The TV was damaged and is covered, but 7.1.9 caps indemnity at a standard equivalent to the 4-year-old 55-inch LED, roughly 520-600. The 50% reduction for no surge protection applies, giving about 280.
The cables were not shown to be physically damaged (4.2.4, 7.1.5). Reference cases put similar lines near zero.
No physical damage is established to the bracket, so it is not an affected item under 7.1.5. Reference cases put it at or near zero.
No damage is shown to the remote, so it is not an affected item under 4.2.4 and 7.1.5.
The console was switched off and unplugged, so it was not affected by the surge. 4.2.4 and 7.1.5 exclude it.
7.1.8(b) excludes carriage and delivery charges for replacement property.
7.1.8(c) excludes fitting and installing replacement property.
This is the contractor's own diagnostic and documentation work (7.1.8(e)) and relates to the service/liability arrangement in 11.2 (7.1.8(f)). It is not a repair cost.

items.description: Wiring safety check of distribution board
items.rationale: The check is on unaffected building wiring (7.1.5) and is a general inspection, not a repair cost (7.1.8(a)).
Under 7.1.8(d), the attendance charge follows the invoice work, and none of this invoice's work is indemnifiable. The charge is therefore not payable.
